summary: Projections over GGUF Q4_0, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K blocks as stored in the file: a host reference equal bit for bit to gguf-py's dequantization and CUDA kernels that decode the same bits in registers for a GEMV over up to 8 rows or an FP32 copy
implementation_scope: A standard-library Python decoder of the five block formats following gguf-py's quants.dequantize operation by operation with FP32 rounding, plus a dense projection and deterministic test blocks; a header-only host/device decoder of eight values at a time with unfused FP32 multiply and subtract; CUDA dequantization and a warp-per-row GEMV for 1 to 8 FP32 activation rows reading the stored blocks directly. Codebook (IQ) formats, Q2_K/Q3_K, quantized activations and tensor-core prompt GEMMs over the blocks are engine work.

agent_guidance.use_when: An engine serves a GGUF checkpoint whose large matrices are Q4_0, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K or Q6_K and decode should read the stored bits without re-encoding them
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The checkpoint uses IQ or other codebook formats, the engine re-encodes weights into its own layout, or a prompt GEMM needs tensor cores over the blocks
provides: The five block layouts and value formulas in data and code, equal bit for bit to gguf-py's quants.dequantize
A host/device decoder of eight values per call with gguf-py's FP32 rounding order and no FMA contraction
A CUDA GEMV over rows of stored blocks for up to 8 activation rows, deterministic per row
A CUDA dequantization to FP32 for prompt GEMMs
Deterministic test blocks shared by the Python and native tests, with recorded digests of gguf-py's output
engine_supplies: The GGUF tensor offsets and shapes (Core's crit_core.model.gguf reads them) and device copies of the blocks
Activations in FP32 and the epilogue after the projection
Batched prompt GEMMs, or a choice to dequantize for them
preserve: One FP32 rounding per multiply and subtract in gguf-py's order
Each row's blocks read in the file's layout
A fixed reduction order per row
adapt: Rows per warp, split-K for short matrices and wider batches
Fusing the dequantization into a tensor-core GEMM tile loader

code_files.purpose: Standard-library decoder equal to gguf-py, dense projection and deterministic test blocks
Block formats and the host/device decoder of eight values with unfused FP32 arithmetic
Dequantization and warp-per-row GEMV kernels for the five formats

requires.hardware: CUDA C++20 on any GPU crit supports; Python 3.11+ standard library for the reference
requires.model: Matrices stored as GGUF Q4_0, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K or Q6_K blocks
requires.workload: Decode or verify steps with 1 to 8 activation rows per projection

contract.input: Device blocks in the file's layout, rows, cols (a multiple of the block's values), FP32 activations [batch][cols] (16-byte aligned), batch 1 to 8
contract.output: FP32 projections [batch][rows], or FP32 values for dequantize
contract.ownership: The engine owns blocks, activations and outputs; launches borrow them on the caller stream
contract.failure: Null buffers, non-positive sizes, a partial block per row, batches outside 1 to 8, unaligned activations or an unknown format return cudaErrorInvalidValue; launch errors are returned. The Python reference raises ValueError for partial blocks
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; Core's GGUF reader supplies tensor offsets and types

dependencies: Python standard library for the reference (gguf-py and numpy only to compare when installed)

validation.host: The Python decoder equals SHA-256 digests of gguf 0.19.0's quants.dequantize on deterministic blocks of each format, and gguf-py itself when installed (checked bit for bit with gguf 0.19.0)
validation.native: The C++ host decoder equals the same digests; the CUDA decode equals the host bit for bit; the GEMV on 37 x 1024 matrices for 1, 3 and 8 rows is within 1e-5 of an FP64 product of the decoded weights
validation.performance: RTX 5090 (1,438 GB/s probed), weights cycling beyond the 96 MB L2, 14336 x 4096 matrix: one activation row 39 us (Q4_0, 841 GB/s of blocks), 45 us (Q8_0, 1,394 GB/s), 37 us (Q4_K, 885 GB/s), 47 us (Q5_K, 855 GB/s), 47 us (Q6_K, 1,023 GB/s); eight rows 97 to 126 us (265 to 645 GB/s), limited by the per-lane activation loop; no claim for other devices or shapes
